verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
The backup job reads SeaweedFS with the read-only `backup` key at `default/backup-minio/seaweedfs` and keeps the `minio/<bucket>/` GCS prefixes.
The `s3` tag, the `s3.lab` backend, the dash tile and the devcontainer alias all point at SeaweedFS.
`minio.lab` stays on MinIO.
The tests pin each of these, and the live evidence covers r3 and r4.
Nothing blocks.
Gates, run by me from the worktree with `loopctl gate stamp`: pass pre_commit, pass cli_tests, pass r1, pass r2, "stamp green: 92314f7a232a53e9953f806b9bff59441217b852592b557a7a61d5f934fe1131".
`kmctl check` (uvx, v0.10.0) reports "all checks passed" and leaves the tree unchanged.

Code read in full: backup-minio.hcl, services.tf (`nomad_job.backup_minio`), haproxy.hcl, minio.hcl, seaweedfs.hcl, tiles.json, bootstrap.sh, .env.example, the CLI comment changes, and every changed test and fixture.
The secret path the job templates matches `vault_kv_secret_v2.backup_seaweedfs_credentials` in deployments/applications/secrets.tf.
It sits under the job's own `default/backup-minio/*` path, which the workloads policy allows.
The `.env.example` access key `admin` matches `default/seaweedfs/admin`.
The applications root's aws provider sets its keys explicitly, so the devcontainer's `AWS_*` variables cannot leak into Terraform.
`git grep 192.168.2.29:9000` finds it only in prometheus.hcl among the jobspecs.
memex.hcl's `${minio_host}:9000` belongs to a job that services.tf has commented out.
r1: test_backup_coverage.py fails if any sync line still reads `minio:`, because the transfer count no longer matches the `seaweedfs:` lines.
It also fails if a bucket is missing, if a destination prefix differs from its source, or if a marker flag is dropped.
The new test pins `provider = SeaweedFS`, the endpoint on 8333 and the key path in services.tf.
Each part of fails_when is covered.
r2: test_s3_cutover.py pins `s3_1 192.168.2.29:8333`, keeps `minio.lab` on 9001, rejects a `minio` tile key, pins the `s3` alias and `.env.example`, and scans every `.hcl` for MinIO's address.
test_seaweedfs_jobspec.py asserts that `s3` is on seaweedfs and not on minio.
The CLI's tag lookup is covered by test_services.py and test_read_commands.py in the cli_tests gate.
r3 (judgment, spike 4): the per-key listing ran before the switch.
It found no missing files in any bucket.
The 725 registry keys missing on SeaweedFS are all zero-byte `dir/` markers, deleted on purpose (spike seaweedfs-cutover-registry/2).
The 5 openviking keys that differ all have SeaweedFS modtimes after the 07:02:45 restore, and OpenViking is that bucket's only writer.
models and datalake are empty.
Met in substance (see Notes).
r4 (judgment, spike 5, plus my own read-only checks): the backup alloc d12af9d8 exited 0.
Afterwards GCS matched SeaweedFS file for file in all four buckets.
I confirmed live that the Consul catalog has `seaweedfs: [s3, http]` and `minio: [http]`, and that `s3.lab` answers `server: SeaweedFS 30GB 4.48`.
The MinIO alloc 4cf10997 still runs at version 14, so the job was updated in place without a restart.
`nomad job history dash` shows the last applications-root submit at 08:12:41 UTC, before the first MinIO count at 08:12:58.
The two counts, 08:12:58 and 08:24:46, are identical and more than 10 minutes apart.
Docs and `.env.example` are as the row requires.
Consistency: docs/reference/gcs-backups.md, edge-routes.md, cli-read-commands.md, the backup how-to, the two explanation pages and the .okf component and node pages match the code.
The comment in services.tf about cross-root apply order is accurate.
None.
r3 departs from the plan's wording.
The check was a boto3 and GCS listing that compares keys and sizes, not `rclone check --one-way` with hashes.
It recorded counts and a coded modtime test rather than named lists.
The key comparison catches the case that matters, a GCS object about to be deleted.
Size-only matching could miss a same-size rewrite, but the sync would overwrite that object with the newer SeaweedFS copy anyway.
The GCS state has moved on since, so there is nothing left to redo.
Three how-tos still teach keyless MinIO access: give-a-job-keyless-minio-access, give-an-aws-sdk-go-service-keyless-minio-access and exchange-a-workload-jwt-for-minio-credentials.
Each says no job uses the MinIO form today.
The minio-removal plan replaces them by name, so I left them to that ticket.
`backup_minio_s3_credentials` is still written and nothing reads it.
The docs say so, and minio-removal deletes it.
